app_info.subtitle: Convert, save and share docs
app_info.description: Convert Markdown to HTML, Confluence, Jira or Slack markup, and HTML, CSV, JSON, plain text, RTF or Evernote exports to Markdown. With a connected TransformPipe account, save, search and read documents, organise them in folders, view versions and summaries, and share documents or folders. Publishing, emailing share notices and deleting ask for confirmation first. Binary files such as Word or PDF are not accepted through these tools.

justifications.read_only_justification: It searches the documentation bundled with the server and returns matching sections; it changes no account data.
justifications.open_world_justification: It reads only the server's own documentation and FAQ text and contacts no external system or person.
justifications.destructive_justification: It does not create, change or delete anything.
justifications.idempotent_justification: The same question returns the same sections and has no side effects.

justifications.read_only_justification: It converts the supplied Markdown to HTML, Confluence storage format, Jira wiki markup or Slack mrkdwn and returns it without saving anything.
justifications.open_world_justification: The conversion runs on the server with local code; it does not publish the result, fetch URLs or contact anyone.
justifications.destructive_justification: No document or account data is created, changed or deleted.
justifications.idempotent_justification: The same input always returns the same output and has no side effects.

justifications.read_only_justification: It converts supplied HTML, CSV, TSV, JSON, plain text, RTF or ENEX text to Markdown and returns it without saving anything.
justifications.open_world_justification: It processes the supplied text with local converters and does not fetch URLs or contact anyone.
justifications.destructive_justification: No document or account data is created, changed or deleted.
justifications.idempotent_justification: The same input always returns the same Markdown and has no side effects.

justifications.read_only_justification: It creates a new document in the connected account, and missing folders when a folder path is given.
justifications.open_world_justification: With share=link it publishes a page anyone with the URL can open, with share=people it emails the given addresses, and saving into a shared folder makes the document visible to that folder's readers; each of these requires confirm=true.
justifications.destructive_justification: It only adds data: it creates a new document (and any missing folders) and never modifies or deletes an existing document.
justifications.idempotent_justification: Each call creates another document with a new id, so repeating a call adds a second copy.

justifications.read_only_justification: It replaces the text of an existing document in the connected account.
justifications.open_world_justification: When the document is shared by link or with named people, its readers see the new text; this case requires confirm=true.
justifications.destructive_justification: It overwrites the document's current text; the previous text is kept as a revision, but only the ten most recent revisions are retained.
justifications.idempotent_justification: Sending the same text again leaves the document unchanged and creates no new revision.

justifications.read_only_justification: It lists or searches the documents in the connected account without modifying them.
justifications.open_world_justification: It reads only the authenticated account's own documents.
justifications.destructive_justification: No document, folder, permission or other account data is changed.
justifications.idempotent_justification: Repeating the call returns the same list and has no side effects.

justifications.read_only_justification: It lists the connected account's folders with document counts and sharing state, and the account's storage totals, without modifying anything.
justifications.open_world_justification: It reads only the authenticated account's own folders and usage.
justifications.destructive_justification: No folder, document, permission or other account data is changed.
justifications.idempotent_justification: Repeating the call returns the same tree and totals and has no side effects.

justifications.read_only_justification: It creates a folder, and any missing parent folders on the given path, in the connected account.
justifications.open_world_justification: A new folder contains no documents and is not published, emailed or sent to any external system.
justifications.destructive_justification: It only adds folders; nothing existing is modified or deleted.
justifications.idempotent_justification: If a folder with the same name already exists in the same place, that folder is returned and nothing new is created.

justifications.read_only_justification: It changes which folder documents in the connected account are filed in, or removes them from all folders.
justifications.open_world_justification: Moving documents into a folder shared by link or with named people makes them readable by that folder's audience; this requires confirm=true.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is deleted or overwritten: a move can be reversed by moving the documents back.
justifications.idempotent_justification: Moving the same documents to the same folder again leaves them where they are.

justifications.read_only_justification: It returns one document from the connected account as Markdown or rendered HTML.
justifications.open_world_justification: It reads only an account document identified by its id, not public content.
justifications.destructive_justification: Reading or rendering the document does not change or remove it.
justifications.idempotent_justification: Repeating the call returns the same document and has no side effects.

justifications.read_only_justification: It generates a summary and stores it on the document as a cache.
justifications.open_world_justification: The document's text is sent to Google's Gemini API, a third-party model, to write the summary.
justifications.destructive_justification: It writes only a derived, cached summary that can be regenerated; the document itself is not changed or deleted.
justifications.idempotent_justification: Without force=true a repeat returns the cached summary, but with force=true each call generates and stores a new summary and counts against the daily limit.

justifications.read_only_justification: It returns a document's earlier revisions and linked versions, or the text of one revision, without adding or changing any.
justifications.open_world_justification: It reads only documents in the authenticated account.
justifications.destructive_justification: No document, revision or link is changed or deleted.
justifications.idempotent_justification: Repeating the call returns the same history and has no side effects.

justifications.read_only_justification: It changes who can open a document: private, anyone with the link, or specified email addresses.
justifications.open_world_justification: Link mode publishes a page reachable by anyone with its URL, and people mode emails user-supplied external addresses; both require confirm=true.
justifications.destructive_justification: Private mode permanently ends the existing link (a later share gets a new URL), and the emails and remove arguments take readers off the list.
justifications.idempotent_justification: Repeating the same share leaves the same state and emails no one again, because only addresses new to the list are notified.

justifications.read_only_justification: It changes who can open a folder and every document in it: private, anyone with the link, or specified email addresses.
justifications.open_world_justification: Link mode publishes the folder as a page reachable by anyone with its URL, and people mode emails user-supplied external addresses; both require confirm=true.
justifications.destructive_justification: Private mode permanently ends the existing folder link (a later share gets a new URL), and the emails and remove arguments take readers off the list.
justifications.idempotent_justification: Repeating the same share leaves the same state and emails no one again, because only addresses new to the list are notified.

justifications.read_only_justification: It renames a folder in the connected account or moves it, with its contents, under another folder or to the top level.
justifications.open_world_justification: Moving a folder under a folder shared by link or with named people makes its documents readable by that audience; this requires confirm=true.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is deleted: a rename or move can be reversed by renaming or moving the folder back.
justifications.idempotent_justification: Repeating the same rename or move leaves the folder as it already is.

justifications.read_only_justification: It deletes one folder from the connected account, and with with_documents=true every document in it.
justifications.open_world_justification: Deletion is limited to the connected account and does not contact anyone or publish anything.
justifications.destructive_justification: The folder is deleted and does not come back; with with_documents=true its documents go to the Trash for 14 days, and a shared folder's link stops working. Every call requires confirm=true.
justifications.idempotent_justification: Once the folder is deleted, repeating the call finds no folder and changes nothing further.

justifications.read_only_justification: It returns the connected account's stored bytes and document count and their limits.
justifications.open_world_justification: It reads only the authenticated account's usage record.
justifications.destructive_justification: It does not change storage, documents or limits.
justifications.idempotent_justification: Repeating the call returns the same figures and has no side effects.

justifications.read_only_justification: With confirm=true it removes one document from the connected account into its Trash, where it is kept for 14 days and then deleted for good.
justifications.open_world_justification: Deletion is limited to one document in the connected account and contacts no one.
justifications.destructive_justification: The document leaves the account and its shared link stops working at once; it can be restored for 14 days, after which it is deleted for good. It requires confirm=true.
justifications.idempotent_justification: Once the document is deleted, repeating the call finds no document and changes nothing further.

justifications.read_only_justification: With an id it puts a deleted document back into the connected account, with its folder, sharing and versions; without one it only lists the Trash.
justifications.open_world_justification: A restored document comes back with the sharing it had: if it was shared by link, that public page opens again for anyone who holds the URL, and named readers can open it again.
justifications.destructive_justification: It removes nothing: it brings back a document exactly as it was before it was deleted.
justifications.idempotent_justification: Once a document is restored it is no longer in the Trash, so repeating the call changes nothing further.

test_cases.description: Convert supplied Markdown into a complete HTML page. No account fixture is needed. Pass if the returned HTML contains a document wrapper, an h1 for Review note, and a list with two items; nothing is saved.
test_cases.user_prompt:
Convert this Markdown into a standalone HTML page with a dark theme: # Review note

- Alpha
- Beta
test_cases.tools_triggered: tp_convert_from_markdown with markdown set to the supplied text, standalone=true and theme=dark
test_cases.expected_output: A complete HTML document containing the Review note heading and Alpha and Beta list items, with no claim that it was saved.

test_cases.description: Convert a small CSV supplied as text into a Markdown table. No account fixture is needed. Pass if both rows and the two column headers appear in the returned table and no document is saved.
test_cases.user_prompt:
Turn this CSV into a Markdown table: name,score
Ada,8
Lin,9
test_cases.tools_triggered: tp_convert_to_markdown with from=csv and source set to the supplied CSV
test_cases.expected_output: A Markdown table with name and score columns and rows Ada/8 and Lin/9, based on the tool result.

test_cases.description: In a dedicated reviewer account with write access, save a private document, find it by name, and read it back. Use a unique filename for each run. Pass if the saved id is used for retrieval and the read result contains the original heading and sentence.
test_cases.user_prompt:
Save this privately as review-note-unique.md: # Review note

The launch checklist is ready. Then find that document in my account and show me what you saved.
test_cases.tools_triggered: tp_save_document with the supplied Markdown, name=review-note-unique.md and private sharing; tp_list_documents with query=review-note-unique; tp_get_document with the saved id
test_cases.expected_output: The document is reported as private; the list includes its id; the retrieved Markdown contains Review note and The launch checklist is ready.

test_cases.description: In a dedicated reviewer account with write access, create a sample document and explicitly publish it by link, then revoke the link. Use only non-sensitive sample text. Pass if publication returns a share URL and revocation returns private mode with the link revoked.
test_cases.user_prompt:
Create a sample document named review-share-unique.md containing '# Sample

Public test content.' Publish it so anyone with the link can read it, then make it private again and tell me whether the link was revoked. I approve both changes.
test_cases.tools_triggered: tp_save_document with the sample Markdown, name=review-share-unique.md, share=link and confirm=true; tp_share_document with the saved id, mode=private
test_cases.expected_output: The first result supplies a link share URL. The second reports private mode and states that the old link is revoked; do not present the old link as still accessible.

test_cases.description: In a connected reviewer account, check account usage and limits. Pass if the response reports stored bytes, document count and per-document limit from the tool result, without inventing a quota value.
test_cases.user_prompt: How much TransformPipe storage am I using, how many documents do I have, and what is the limit for one document?
test_cases.tools_triggered: tp_usage with an empty argument object
test_cases.expected_output: Current stored bytes and document count, each with its limit, plus the per-document Markdown limit, all consistent with tp_usage output.

negative_test_cases.description: The MCP tools cannot accept a binary PDF, and TransformPipe does not claim PDF conversion. Explain the limit without calling a conversion tool or claiming a converted result.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Can TransformPipe convert my PDF into Markdown here?
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Explain that PDF conversion is unsupported by these tools and do not fabricate Markdown from an unseen file.

negative_test_cases.description: The converter accepts supplied source text but cannot fetch a web page by URL. Ask for page HTML or explain how to supply it; do not pass the URL string as if it were HTML.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Fetch https://example.com and convert that web page to Markdown with TransformPipe.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Explain that the MCP converter needs the HTML source and cannot fetch the URL itself.

negative_test_cases.description: The server can delete only one document by id per call and has no bulk-delete tool. Decline an account-wide wipe without looking up ids or issuing deletion calls.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Wipe every document in my TransformPipe account in one operation, without showing me what would be deleted.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Explain that there is no bulk-delete operation and that each deletion requires a specific document and explicit confirmation.
